utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see Tuta doing at that time in connection with Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evening before that -- on the eve of the liberation of Orlovac, he invited me to Siroki Brijeg. And there in the Convicts Battalion unit, they showed me the plan of the attack against that feature. And then they asked me that the next morning -- they asked me to be present the next morning when that plan was to be put in action, and I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred just now a couple of times to "they." Who were the "they" that you were talking about? You said "they showed me the plan of the attack."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, I can of course say that it was Ivan Andabak or that it was Hrkac whose nickname was Cikota. And then I'd stopped there because it was simply too long ago. And I cannot really say with certainty who else happened to be in a room one evening. But it was the Convicts Battalion. It was Mr. Andabak, and Mr. Mladen Naletilic was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you please assist us, sir, with -- give the first name of the man Hrkac, nickname, I believe, Cikota. But just for the record, if you could give us his first name.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Cikota.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you talked about seeing the attack plan the night before. Did you see then -- what did you see the next day? You said you were asked to be at the attack. What did you see then?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't request that. They asked me to be there, invited me to be there. I saw a well-prepared and well-executed successful operation which ended in the liberation of the right bank of the Neretva. It drove away the Chetniks from the remaining elevations and significantly reduced the number of people killed in that area by Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... carried out this action?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if in addition to the Convicts Battalion there was somebody else. I do know that that battalion took part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It included the Convicts Battalion, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I do not know who else was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I did not pay any attention at that time, nor do I do it today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see Tuta do on the day of the attack itself?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stood next to me. That is, I stood next to him. Or rather, we stood there together. We were standing there observing, following the action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you standing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to a house, a small one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you know, just generally speaking, were you in a particular village, were you on a geographic feature? Where were you approximately standing along with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer that question exactly and precisely, you would all need to have before you Mostar and hills and the position of Mostar. I was standing on the ground near that feature, at a place from which -- which commanded a good view of that area and was not exposed in a manner in which you could get easily killed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay with Tuta throughout the duration of that action?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards, when we saw that the action was getting ahead very successfully and when the information arrived from the guys who were -- who had gone forward, that the Chetniks were fleeing, then on my own initiative, having assessed the situation, I ordered Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac, who at that time was a commander in Mostar, or the commander in Mostar, and all the soldiers of the Croat Defence Council towards Capljina, to launch a forceful offensive in the direction of the Neretva, and there, owing to the successful Orlovac operation, at 8.00 or 9.00 in the evening, we chased away the Chetniks and the Yugoslav People's Army and they never managed to put fire to two large plants, the aluminium plant and the sock plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to cut you off there because it goes far beyond the question I asked you. Who did Tuta report to that day as his superior? Was he reporting? Were you there standing next to him as his superior officer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What you are trying to suggest, Mr. Prosecutor, did not happen, and I'm sorry, I have to say that. I simply am trying to explain that it wasn't such an army as you are persistently trying to show, that there was an organised army, that there was a structured army, such as you find in the armies of well-organised states which had been set up 500 or 600 years ago. I shall keep repeating the truth about it, about how it really was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not have individual -- so I put it to you, sir, you did not have individual soldiers acting at random on that day, and you indicated a moment ago that at least quite possibly there was even another unit besides the Convicts Battalion involved in that. Now, who was organising this attack and who did Tuta report to, if not to you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody needed to report to me, because I could see what happened, and the form of reporting about successful operations, we did not have that at the time, and Mr. Naletilic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we will come back to it tomorrow if we have to. Who was Mr. Naletilic's superior at the time of the attack on Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your superior on that day?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, regarding that decision, nobody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Final question, then: As of that time, or perhaps any time -- well, let's take it one step at a time. As of, then, late May, early June, 1992, what is your answer to this Chamber, sir, about what was Naletilic's relationship to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. In what sense? Do you mean was he within the HVO structure?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he part of the HVO or was he just running his private army?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, as far as I know, the Convicts Battalion was under the command of Mr. Andabak, Ivan Andabak, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, once again, you, I submit to you, intentionally have not answered my question. Was the Convicts Battalion part of the HVO in late May, early June, 1992? I'll put it that way, slightly different, to you, if that assists you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that I do not -- that I decline to answer the question, Mr. Prosecutor. The number of units, the number of independent units, the number of organised village teams, was so large, in addition to HOS, that I simply cannot give you a precise answer to that question. I can give you a precise answer to that question only with regard to the time when I was commander of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I suggest we can stop there for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, I'm afraid we have to call you back tomorrow. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, would you please inform us how long you are going to take at tomorrow's sitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At least all day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to sit late tomorrow afternoon again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. That's up to the Chamber, whether you want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to give us approximately how many hours so that we could arrange -- we could decide whether we could sit tomorrow afternoon or not, because it is the Chamber's intention to let this witness go to spend the weekend at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If that's the Chamber's wishes, then I suspect that between my continued questions, redirect examination, and presumably the Judges' questions, I suspect that we will be here until late tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My question is how long your cross-examination will take?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would say at least four hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we will rise until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, excuse me, before that, this witness does not mind -- as far as I could understand, this witness will not mind staying here over the weekend, because we are working so hard, and if we again have to work until 7.00 this Friday? The witness does not mind. He can resume on Monday. Your Honours, I don't know how many times do I have to repeat this and how many times I have to ask you that. We are really exhausted. Last week we worked until 7.00. This Friday, we shall work until 7.00, when the witness can stay over the weekend? Let him stay, even, of course, it will complicate matters for us further with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, but what can we do about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I have to say that we are far behind schedule. During the first two weeks, we only had two witnesses. We are far behind schedule. We are very worried about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. I will take the liberty to say the following: I think that we are the only ones who are working very, very fast. I am looking at other cases who started on the same day as we did. The Prosecutors have not gone through 14 witnesses yet. And we have, I think, finished a large chunk of our work and we are working very fast. And witnesses are as they are. There are many objections. We work only in the mornings and we waste -- we spend a lot of time watching tapes and objections and apologies, with all due respect, but I think that this Chamber, this case, is moving ahead very quickly when compared to other cases in this Tribunal. And even if such witnesses take more time, I think it is -- it does serve the interests of truth. And I really do not object to -- of course, whilst respecting your rulings, but I have nothing against my learned friend examining this witness as long as he likes, because that will be in the interests of the truth, even though he should have done that six years ago, but what can we do now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, there is no comparison between various cases before this Tribunal. The different cases have different situations, as you know. But what I am concerned is that we are far behind schedule. We have our schedule for this case. That's why we denied your motion for a break. Anyway, we will rise until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
